topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting it to earlier histopathology practicals and outlining the learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumour virology and experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical discovery of transforming viruses and cellular proto-oncogenes alongside the laboratory assays used to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification and mutation mechanisms of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define oncogenes, tumour suppressor genes, and driver mutations, illustrating how different mutational mechanisms deregulate key cell cycle controls such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms, types, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumour progression, hereditary predisposition, and tumour evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cumulative mutational acquisition drives cancer progression, how inherited germline mutations accelerate tumour development, and how tumours adapt under selective pressure.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session with a recap of the learning outcomes, recommended reading, and a preview of the next lecture.
